Suki AI

Senior Full Stack AI Engineer

This role was deeply product-focused, not just model-focused.

I worked on AI features that clinicians used in real patient workflows. The bar was high: if output was unclear or unreliable, people would not use it.

The Real Scenario

A clinician has back-to-back visits and only a short gap before the next patient.

They still need complete, accurate notes. If documentation takes too long, care time gets squeezed and burnout rises.

Our product had to feel like a trusted assistant, not another tool to babysit.

What I Owned

  • Built and improved core documentation features for clinical note generation and summarization.
  • Worked on speech-to-structured-data flows so spoken context became usable documentation.
  • Improved retrieval and context quality so output reflected real clinical scenarios.
  • Partnered closely with product and design to make outputs understandable for non-technical users.
  • Drove iteration loops using feedback from real workflows, not synthetic test cases only.

Scrappy Startup Moments

1. Accuracy had to improve without slowing delivery

We needed to ship quickly, but poor output quality would erode trust immediately.

I prioritized high-impact quality fixes first, then layered deeper improvements behind clear evaluation checkpoints.

2. Real-world edge cases were everywhere

Different providers documented differently. Visit styles varied by specialty.

I helped make the pipeline more adaptable so the product stayed useful across messy, real-world variation.

3. Cross-functional ownership was required

This was not a "throw it over the wall" environment.

I worked across backend, AI behavior, and product UX details so the end experience felt coherent and dependable.

Human Impact

  • Providers spent less energy on repetitive documentation tasks.
  • Teams got cleaner, more consistent notes to work from.
  • The product felt practical for daily use, not just impressive in demos.

What I'd Build Next

  • Better per-specialty quality controls and explainability.
  • Stronger in-product feedback loops to improve output over time.
  • More automation across follow-up actions after note completion.
